questions.q: She is ___ tall as her sister.

questions.explanation: 'Not as ... as' compares two unequal things.
questions.q: This book is ___ interesting as that one.
He is ___ strong as his brother.
My house is ___ big as yours.

questions.explanation: 'Too + adjective + to' means more than enough.
questions.q: This coffee is ___ hot to drink.
He isn't old ___ to drive.

questions.explanation: The pattern is 'as + adjective + as', never 'than'.
options: She is as tall than me.
She is so tall as me.
She is as tall as me.
She is as taller as me.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
I don't have ___ money to buy a car.
This exam was ___ difficult as the last one.
The box is ___ heavy to lift.
She speaks English ___ fluently as a native speaker.
He's not tall ___ to reach the shelf.

options: He is as fast as me.
She is too tired to walk.
They are as happy as us.
questions.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
My coffee is ___ hot as yours.
The water isn't warm ___ to swim.
He ran ___ fast as the wind.
I'm not strong ___ to open this jar.
This room is ___ cold as outside.

questions.explanation: 'Too + adjective + to + verb' is the pattern.
questions.q: She's too young ___ married.

questions.explanation: Questions with equal comparison use 'as ... as'.
questions.q: Is your English ___ good as mine?
